passage: To understand triangles, we must look at their properties carefully. First, consider the sides. For any three lengths to form a triangle, the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third side. If the sum equals the third side, the lines will just lie flat on each other, failing to form a triangle. Second, consider the angles. The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of the triangle's size or shape. If you know two angles, you find the third by subtracting their sum from 180. Third, consider the lines inside. An altitude is a line segment from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side, but it does not necessarily bisect that side. A median, however, connects a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side, always staying inside the triangle. Finally, look at the exterior angle. When you extend one side of a triangle, the exterior angle formed is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles, not the one right next to it. Remember, the Pythagoras property, which relates the sides as a² + b² = c², applies exclusively to right-angled triangles, not to every triangle you encounter.

items.evidence: If the sum equals the third side, the lines will just lie flat on each other, failing to form a triangle.
items.q: Three sticks measure 4 cm, 6 cm and 10 cm. What happens when Meera joins them?
options: They lie flat and make no triangle
They make a very thin triangle
They make a right-angled triangle
They make a triangle with a bent side
items.explain: The two short sticks add up to exactly the longest, so the sticks lie flat and form no triangle.

wrong.why: thinks equal sum still gives a triangle
links the sum 4 + 6 = 10 to a right triangle
imagines the sticks can bend to fit

items.evidence: The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is always exactly 180 degrees, regardless of the triangle's size or shape.
items.q: Asha draws a huge triangle and Ravi draws a tiny one. What can we say about their angle sums?
options: Both sums are the same
Asha's sum is much greater
Ravi's sum is much greater
Both sums are the same only if right-angled
items.explain: The angle sum of every triangle is 180 degrees, whatever its size or shape.

wrong.why: thinks a bigger triangle has a bigger sum
thinks a smaller triangle has a bigger sum
thinks 180 degrees holds only for right triangles

items.evidence: An altitude is a line segment from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side, but it does not necessarily bisect that side.
items.q: How is an altitude different from a median of a triangle?
options: It meets the side at a right angle
It always meets the side at its midpoint
It is always the slanted side itself
It can lie outside the triangle
items.explain: An altitude is perpendicular to the opposite side, while a median goes to the midpoint of that side.

wrong.why: thinks an altitude must bisect the side
thinks the altitude is a slanted side
thinks a median can lie outside

items.evidence: When you extend one side of a triangle, the exterior angle formed is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles, not the one right next to it.
items.q: In a triangle, two interior angles are 50 and 60 degrees. What is the exterior angle at the third vertex?
options: 110 degrees
70 degrees
130 degrees
180 degrees
items.explain: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so 50 + 60 = 110 degrees.

wrong.why: subtracts the sum from 180 and stops
thinks it equals the adjacent angle, 130 + 50
confuses it with the full angle sum

items.evidence: Remember, the Pythagoras property, which relates the sides as a² + b² = c², applies exclusively to right-angled triangles, not to every triangle you encounter.
items.q: Sides of a triangle are 5, 6 and 8 cm. What does a² + b² = c² tell us?
options: It does not hold, so the triangle is not right-angled
It holds, so the triangle is right-angled
It holds for every triangle, so it tells nothing
It fails because 5 + 6 is greater than 8
items.explain: 25 + 36 = 61, not 64, so the property fails and the triangle is not right-angled.

wrong.why: assumes the property must work for these sides
thinks the property holds for every triangle
mixes it up with the side-sum check
